claim: Connectivity architecture contains predictive information about neurotransmitter identity within the examined Drosophila olfactory neuron population.
Synaptic-weight distribution features made substantial predictive contributions in the evaluated models.
Outgoing and incoming connectivity features contributed substantially to prediction within the evaluated feature set.
Cell-type-grouped cross-validation provides a stricter assessment of generalization across canonical cell types.
The observed relationship is universal across Drosophila neurons.
The result is established to generalize across brain regions or species.
Individual connectivity features are independently causal.
